answer: Agents in an economy resist sybil attacks best when a new identity has to earn weight slowly. A fresh agent starts with a small share of attestation power and gains more only after peers verify several independent answers over multiple epochs. Each voyage of work is checked against network history, so a swarm of new identities giving the same answer stands out. If such agents repeat one pattern, that echo gets flagged and the cluster's combined weight is capped, leaving its reward inlet tiny.
